label: Google Cloud Identity Platform
note: Google Cloud Identity Platform (the enterprise upgrade of Firebase Authentication). Supports SMS and TOTP as MFA second factors; email verification is required before MFA enrollment.

questions.label: Product tier
questions.text: Is the project upgraded to Identity Platform, or running base Firebase Authentication?

guidance.text: **Review.** Base Firebase Authentication lacks MFA, blocking functions, user activity/audit logging, SAML/OIDC, and multi-tenancy. Upgrade to Firebase Auth with Identity Platform to access MFA and enterprise controls needed for the checks below.
**Good.** Identity Platform unlocks MFA, blocking functions, audit logging, and multi-tenancy.

questions.label: MFA second factors
questions.text: Which MFA second factors are enabled? (select all that apply)

guidance.text: **Good.** TOTP is a solid second factor. Enforce email verification before enrollment (MFA requires a verified email) and encourage users to register a backup factor, since Identity Platform has no built-in second-factor recovery.

**Review.** SMS is exposed to SIM-swap; prefer TOTP where possible. Keep the fully-blocking SMS region policy and the reCAPTCHA verifier enabled to limit phone-auth abuse, and require verified emails before enrollment.
**GAP.** Enable MFA (TOTP and/or SMS). Require verified emails first (MFA depends on it), and prompt users to register a backup factor, as there is no built-in recovery for a lost second factor.

questions.label: Abuse / account protection
questions.text: Is bot and abuse protection (reCAPTCHA Enterprise) plus Google's compromised-account protection in use?

guidance.text: **GAP.** Enable reCAPTCHA-based bot/abuse protection on sign-up and sign-in, and rely on Identity Platform's integration with Google's threat signals to detect compromised accounts. This is a core account-takeover defense.
**Review.** Extend protection to all auth entry points (sign-up, sign-in, password reset, phone verification) so attackers cannot target the least-protected flow.
**Good.** Bot/abuse and compromised-account protection are active. Monitor auth activity logs for anomalies.

questions.label: Blocking functions
questions.text: Are blocking functions used to enforce policy at authentication events (e.g. email-domain restrictions, custom checks)?

guidance.text: **Good.** Blocking functions (beforeCreate / beforeSignIn) enforce policy server-side. Verify tokens server-side with the Admin SDK and validate issuer, audience, and expiry.

**Note.** Blocking functions (beforeCreate / beforeSignIn) let you enforce email verification, domain allowlists, and custom access rules that clients cannot bypass. Consider them for policy enforcement, and always verify tokens server-side with the Admin SDK.
